cohort: The study included 460 mothers with high HBV viremia (HBV DNA > 2 x 10^5 IU/ml) and their 462 infants who received timely immunoprophylaxis but whose mothers did not receive antiviral therapy.
finding: Elective cesarean section and bottle-feeding do not reduce mother-to-child transmission of HBV in infants born to high viremic mothers who did not receive antiviral therapy, given timely infant immunoprophylaxis.
mod_finding: The MTCT rate in vaginally delivered infants was similar to that in infants delivered via elective cesarean section, indicating no significant reduction in MTCT by mode of birth.
followup_time: up to 14 months (HBsAg tested at 7-14 month age, average 9.9 +- 2.4 months)
